# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — first capability from the empty seed: literal-value contract + openpyxl method + inspect→solve→verify→finish procedure
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md (new): role; "How your output is graded" (no recalc → write computed literals even for "write a formula" asks; correct types; keep pre-filled correct cells; use the displayed value of formula cells); "Working with the workbook" (openpyxl load/set/save, data_only read copy, no pandas to_excel, preview index 0 = Excel row 2, read inputs in code, float tolerance); "Understanding the task" (read labels/examples/neighbour formulas, reproduce examples, per-row shape, literal instructions).
  - task_template.md (new, overrides the built-in): same fields; replaces "once that file exists, you are done" with a 4-step procedure: inspect with real addresses → solve with literals → verify by printing answer_position → finish with a no-code reply.
- Expected effect: cluster A (formulas; ~13 tasks, 7 already correct once recalculated) is the main gain. B/C/E (coordinates, examples, pandas clobbering; ~8 tasks) partial. D ends the 30-round resubmit loops. Safe because all 18 passing tasks already write literal values. The procedure only adds an inspection round and an earlier stop.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- Not yet cracked: semantic misreads (43436 date boundaries, 80-42 large consolidation) need more than general rules.
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration: read the new traces for tasks still failing after literal values. Likely wrong logic or ambiguous semantics; consider a worked example of "reproduce the example rows first".

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.680 Δ=+0.230 · fixed={37378, 46897, 53383, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569} · broke={142-12, 2768, 382-10, 38462, 395-36, 402-43, 416-15, 45635, 463-17, 47798, 48588, 560-12, 9726} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## SpreadsheetBench grading mechanics (verified from score blobs + adapter source, not yet by a RESULT)
- Grader metric is hard_no_recalc: formula cells written by openpyxl score as empty. 7/22 seed failures were right once recalculated. Writing computed literals is the top lever (cand_0001).
- A no-code reply ends the rollout once the output exists. The built-in template never said so, so agents looped for 30 rounds.
- The preview is pandas read_excel with the default header: index 0 = Excel row 2. That is a source of off-by-one errors.
- Promising but not yet tried: a minimal worked example of inspecting and matching pre-filled example cells.

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (empty seed)
- Strategy: read the score blob's raw metrics (test_case_results vs test_case_results_no_recalc) first. That separated "right logic, wrong artifact" from "wrong logic" immediately. Then 3 parallel diagnosis subagents over the remaining 15 traces.
- Both editable files were used: knowledge/contract went into prompt.md, the ordered procedure into task_template.md (it replaces the built-in "you are done" line).
- Next: once literals are in place, remaining failures should be semantic. Cluster those by misread type.

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001
- INSTRUCTIONS.md says both prompt.md and task_template.md are editable, but the empty seed ships no task_template.md. The agent has to find the adapter to learn the built-in text and the placeholder contract. Ship the built-in template as a file in the empty seed (or quote it in INSTRUCTIONS).

files.text:
# PROCESS — cand_0001 (empty seed → first capability)

Starting state: prompt.md empty (no system message), no task_template.md (adapter built-in template, which ends "once that file exists, you are done"). Val 0.450 (18/40). No environment faults found: every trace executed code, and each failure has a task-level cause.

Grader fact verified in the trace score blobs: `reward_metric: hard_no_recalc`. Seven tasks have `test_case_results=[1]` but `test_case_results_no_recalc=[0]`, so they are correct once recalculated and fail only because they wrote formulas.

## Ranked issue list
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula written instead of value (grader doesn't recalc) | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942, 55979, 56563, 9569, 53647, 54144, 37456 (+267-18 edited formula text) | "How do I write a formula…" is answered by writing a formula string; it reads back empty or as error text | KNOWLEDGE / CONTRACT | output contract + reason (prompt.md) |
| 2 | B. No inspection: coordinates taken from the pandas preview (row off by one), layout/axes/examples ignored | 227-40, 59196, 50768, 53647, 39046, 43436, 48527 | acts in round 1 without reading real cells; preview index 0 = Excel row 2 | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure step 1 (template) + knowledge line on the preview offset + "reproduce examples" rule |
| 3 | C. pandas to_excel rewrite clobbers sheet/other cells | 227-40, 48527, 50768, 80-42, 39046 | round-trips the whole sheet | KNOWLEDGE (method) | concrete openpyxl idiom (prompt.md) |
| 4 | D. No verification, 30-round resubmit loop | 51-12, 53647, 54144, 9569, 80-42, 227-40, 39046, 43436 (also many passing tasks loop harmlessly) | built-in template: "once that file exists, you are done" but no way to finish is stated; agent resends the same code | STRUCTURE | template steps 3–4: verify by printing answer_position, then finish with a no-code reply |
| 5 | E. Pre-filled example / correct cells in the target overwritten | 48527, 39046, 54144 | treats the whole range as blank | CONTRACT | "keep cells that are already correct; examples are part of expected" |
| 6 | F. Float threshold comparison | 51-12 | 100*1.1 ≠ 110 | KNOWLEDGE | one tolerance line |
| 7 | G. Formula-cell text edited instead of displayed value | 267-18 | loaded without data_only | KNOWLEDGE | data_only read / normal write idiom |

## Changes made
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | tighten output contract + reason | prompt.md "How your output is graded" | grader reads stored values → compute a formula's result and write the literal; applies to every "create a formula" task | all 18 passing tasks already write literals (they pass no_recalc) |
| A/E/type | contract | prompt.md | literal types, exact source spelling; keep correct pre-filled cells | passing tasks already comply |
| C/G | knowledge (method) | prompt.md "Working with the workbook" | openpyxl load→set→save, data_only second copy, no to_excel | passing pandas tasks (e.g. 31628) write the same values; openpyxl preserves more, so it changes the method but not the graded values |
| B | knowledge + restructure | prompt.md + template step 1 | preview offset stated; inspect real cells before solving; examples must be reproduced | passing tasks gain one inspection round; they have ≥25 rounds spare |
| D | ordered procedure | task_template.md steps 1–4 | replaces "once that file exists, you are done" with inspect → solve → verify → finish (no code block) | adapter stops on a no-code reply once the answer exists, so passing tasks end earlier with the same file |
| F | knowledge | prompt.md | float tolerance idiom | only affects threshold comparisons |
| literal-instruction | rule | prompt.md | "append after existing data even if it looks done" (80-42) | bounded to append tasks |

## Verify-the-fix
- trace 46897/55049/9569/56563…: final code `ws['I3'] = '=COUNTIF(...)'`; feedback says "answer cells hold FORMULAS". The new contract says a "how do I write a formula" task expects the value, and to compute it in Python. 9569's own debug helper `get_earliest_value` already computed the right values.
- trace 59196/53647/227-40: hardcoded rows taken from the preview (header on row 2 / C4 vs C5 / iloc[13] = row 15). Step 1 now requires printing real openpyxl addresses before solving, and prompt.md states the index-0 = row 2 offset (checked against the adapter: `read_excel` default header, extent reported as `rows 1-{nrows+1}`).
- trace 39046/48527/43436/50768: the example cells F2:F4, D2 "Apple", column H, and F14 went unread. Step 1 prints them, and the rule says to reproduce the examples before filling the rest.
- trace 51-12/54144: the same code was sent about 28 times until round 30, with no print. Step 3 prints answer_position; step 4 names the exit (plain-text reply). The adapter code confirms a no-code reply ends the loop once solution_code exists.
- trace 267-18: `//=CONCATENATE(` written. The data_only rule means the displayed value gets edited instead.
- trace 80-42: pandas ExcelWriter rewrite, and the agent decided "already consolidated". The openpyxl idiom and the literal-instruction rule address both.
- Template placeholder contract validated with the adapter's `_task_template_error` → None, and it renders.

## Process & features used
- 3 parallel read-only diagnosis subagents (5 traces each). I read the formula cluster and a passing 30-round trace myself.
- No prior iterations exist (RUNMAP is empty; rejected.jsonl is empty).

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The literal-values contract, the openpyxl edit idiom, and the verify-then-finish-with-no-code procedure.

## Deliberately skipped
- 43436's month-end boundary semantics (ambiguous; needs gold). 80-42 is a large consolidation task, and only the general rules are applied to it.
- Excel-365 function lists: moot once values are computed in Python.

{{TARGET_READER}}

{{FOCUS_SUMMARY}}

{{EMPTY_SEED}}

GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `{{CAP_BRIEF}}` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
knows.** When the agent has the rule and skips it anyway, adding a second sentence saying
the same thing changes nothing — you must change the STRUCTURE that makes it skippable
(see the levers below): make the step unavoidable and ordered, make the contract explicit,
or give a worked example it can pattern-match. Prose is for genuine KNOWLEDGE gaps (a
fact / format / criterion the agent cannot derive) and for STRUCTURE that changes what the
agent does — not for repetition or emphasis.

1. **REAL** — it targets a cluster that is FAILING in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`
